Robert Thomas was named the NHL's first star of the week after a 10-point run that ended Nov. 22, and it stretched into a five-game point streak with nine assists. He is the Blues' engine at 20 minutes a night: 25 points in 25 games, 20 of them assists, with seven on the power play. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking backs up the passer label, with 10.1 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 94th percentile among forwards.

Here's the catch. With Thomas on the ice, St. Louis has scored 13.3 more goals than its chances deserve (expected goals measure chance quality), and that cushion is padding his line. His own shooting has gone the other way: five goals on 6.31 expected. The process is real; he drove play last season by Evolving-Hockey's measure, worth 2.8 wins, 20th among forwards. Our numbers project 82 points, in a range of 69 to 95. Watch whether the assists keep coming once the bounces even out.
headline: Robert Thomas's big week, and the luck under it
